youtubeTitle: Build with Bob: NotebookLM Clone Part 1 (Intro)
youtubeDescription:
Building software in today's AI assisted world is quite exciting and IBM's Bob is a wonderful agentic coding partner. Combine that with a local, open source RAG platform like OpenRAG and you have yourself a solid stack to build some amazing applications. 

Watch Tejas Kumar, David Jones-Gilardi, and Bob team up to build new features for their open source NotebookLM clone using OpenRAG. 

From AI-powered spec coding and architectural decisions to live debugging and feature development, you'll get an inside look at what modern AI-assisted software engineering actually looks like.

youtubeTitle: Building with Bob: Walfly Wearables App
youtubeDescription:
Tejas and David continue their journey to create wearable app "Walfly" using IBM's AI coding IDE Bob. 

Last week we had some serious progress on Walfly and finally pushed past the audio transcription challenges we experienced previously. Expo mobile app emulation is working and we generally have a functioning app. 

Now it's time to to refine and really work on the UX and usefulness of the app. UX design, Expo debugging, recording checkpoints, and the messy reality of shipping a real app with AI coding agents. Lets go!

youtubeTitle: Building with Bob: Walfly Wearables App
youtubeDescription:
Last episode, Tejas and David improved the UX design and tackled lots of Expo debugging.

Now that the app is stable on both web and mobile, we'll move our focus to handling recording checkpoints for long recordings and introduce some new tools for managing our agents.

But first!

In this episode we improve the app’s mobile experience, compare AI coding reviews from Bob and Xavier, troubleshoot keyboard and layout issues, and plan audio chunking and cloud hosting for the next episode. Looks like we had some "completeness" work to do before moving on.

youtubeTitle: Building with Bob: Walfly Wearables App
youtubeDescription:
Last episode, we explored AI-assisted code reviews with Bob and Xavier, fine-tuned the mobile UI, and laid the groundwork for managing our agents asynchronously.

Now, we're diving headfirst into audio chunking and live recording checkpoints for walfly!

In this episode, we use Bob and Xavier to plan and build a separate, ephemeral ASR service for wallfly, then test audio chunking and uncover issues to tackle next. Along the way, they discuss coordinating AI agents with human teammates, and the privacy, consent, and security questions that come with recording conversations.
